class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

class FactChecker:

        """

        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """

class Questions(BaseModel):

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.

<self expr="doc(type(self))">
class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
</system_prompt>

<self expr="doc(type(self))">
class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has

    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:

        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.

        objects.

        """

class EvidenceStance(Enum):

    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence
        contradicts it. Return NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted, including a named
        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to classify.
            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """
## Referenced Types
class Evidence(BaseModel):
    finding: Finding  # What one scout concluded from its search.
    passage: str = ''  # The retrieved text the finding was assessed against; reusable as evidence for other questions.

class EvidenceStance(Enum):
    SUPPORTS = 'SUPPORTS'
    CONTRADICTS = 'CONTRADICTS'
    INSUFFICIENT = 'INSUFFICIENT'

class Finding(BaseModel):
    question: str = ''  # The independently investigated question, copied exactly.
    answer: str = ''  # A concise answer grounded only in the search results.
    source: str = ''  # The exact Wikipedia title and URL supporting the answer, or an empty string when none was found.
    excerpt: str = ''  # The shortest exact excerpt from the search results that supports the answer, or an empty string.
    stance: EvidenceStance = <EvidenceStance.INSUFFICIENT: 'INSUFFICIENT'>  # SUPPORTS if the search results establish the part of the claim this question is about, CONTRADICTS if they establish that it is false, INSUFFICIENT only if they do not answer the question.

class Questions(BaseModel):
    """The analyzer's fan-out for one round. A named model rather than a bare list[str]: NOOA"""

    questions: list[str]  # Between one and maximum_questions self-contained questions, each usable verbatim as an English Wikipedia search query; empty when nothing is left to research.

class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: VerdictLabel = <VerdictLabel.NEED_MORE: 'NEED_MORE'>  # SUPPORTED only when the evidence supports every material part of the claim; NOT_SUPPORTED when a material part is contradicted by reliable evidence; NEED_MORE only when a material part has no evidence either way and another search could plausibly settle it.
    rationale: str = ''  # A concise cross-document explanation of the verdict that names every unsupported or contradicted part.
    sources: list[str]  # Only the exact non-empty source strings from the evidence that were used for the verdict.

class VerdictLabel(Enum):
    SUPPORTED = 'SUPPORTED'
    NOT_SUPPORTED = 'NOT_SUPPORTED'
    NEED_MORE = 'NEED_MORE'
</self>

        """
    async def assess_evidence(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], question: str, search_results: str) -> Finding:
        """
        Assess only the supplied search results, using earlier evidence solely to resolve references
        in the question. Return one Finding. Copy its question exactly. Judge only the part of the

class FactChecker:
    """
    A HoVer-style multi-hop fact checker: decompose the claim into independent questions,
    research them in parallel, combine all evidence into a verdict, repeat when more is needed.
    """

    async def decompose_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence], maximum_questions: int) -> Questions:
        """
        Propose between one and maximum_questions self-contained factual questions that can be
        researched independently and in parallel in this round, each one usable verbatim as an
        English Wikipedia search query. With no evidence yet, cover every entity, relation,
        comparison, date, and quantity needed to decide the whole claim. With evidence present,
        target only the parts whose findings are INSUFFICIENT or in conflict; follow-up questions
        may use entities and answers already established by earlier findings (multi-hop), and must
        not repeat a question that already has a SUPPORTS or CONTRADICTS finding. Do not answer the
        questions.
        
        Args:
            claim: The complete claim to verify.
            evidences: Every finding collected in earlier rounds of this fact check, oldest first; empty in the first round.
            maximum_questions: The hard upper bound on independent fan-out branches this round.
        """
    async def verify_claim(self, claim: str, evidences: list[Evidence]) -> Verdict:
        """
        Apply HoVer's decision rule to the claim and all evidence together, reading the findings'
        answers and passages, not only their stance labels. Return SUPPORTED only if reliable
        evidence collectively establishes every material part of the claim and no reliable evidence

        entity or attribute that the evidence shows to be wrong. A retrieved Wikipedia article about
        an entity that lists its roles or attributes and does not mention a claimed one is evidence
        against that part, not missing evidence. Return NEED_MORE only when a material part has no
        evidence either way and a further search could plausibly settle it; when the same fact has
        already been searched for repeatedly without result, decide on the balance of the evidence.
        Explain the cross-document reasoning, and cite only source strings present in the evidence
        objects.

            evidences: The complete set of findings collected so far, oldest first.
        """

Over millennia, through the process of natural selection, plants have evolved the means to produce a vast and complicated array of chemical compounds to deter herbivores. Many of the known plant defense compounds primarily defend against consumption by insects, though other animals, including humans, that consume such plants may also experience negative effects, ranging from mild discomfort to death.

Title: Cicutoxin
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicutoxin
Excerpt: Cicutoxin is a naturally-occurring poisonous chemical compound produced by several plants from the family Apiaceae including water hemlock (Cicuta species) and water dropwort (Oenanthe crocata).  The compound contains polyene, polyyne, and alcohol functional groups and is a structural isomer of oenanthotoxin (also found in water dropwort) and bupleurotoxin (found in Bupleurum longiradiatum).  All of these belong to the C17-polyacetylenes chemical class.
It causes death by respiratory paralysis resulting from disruption of the central nervous system. It is a potent, noncompetitive antagonist of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptor. In humans, cicutoxin rapidly produces symptoms of nausea, emesis and abdominal pain, typically within 60 minutes of ingestion. This can lead to tremors, seizures, and death. LD50(mouse; i.p.) ~9 mg/kg
